summary.title: Technical Writing for Developers
summary.one_liner: Learn practical writing habits for developers, covering English grammar basics, code comments, pull requests, bug reports, client communication, microcopy, and accessible markup.
takeaways: Write code comments that add context and explain why, not what the code obviously does, and update them together with the code.
Write PR titles in imperative tense that say what changes, and put the why and details in the PR body; keep PRs small.
Make bug reports reproducible with environment details, steps, expected vs actual behavior, and screenshots or recordings.
Use active voice, clear tone, and questions rather than accusations when communicating with clients and users.
Write error messages (microcopy) without jargon or blame, and use semantic HTML and alt text for accessibility.
summary.summary: This CSS-Tricks article argues that writing skills matter as much as coding skills for developers. It opens with a short primer on English grammar, parts of speech, tone, and active versus passive voice, then moves into practical advice. The practical sections cover code comments, pull request titles and bodies, bug reporting, client communication, microcopy for error messages, and accessible markup. Advice is illustrated with short code and template examples.
